messages:
Alex: Heads up — deploybot rejected the push for release/1.24.2; attestation timestamp mismatch on the manifest.
deploy-bot: publish rejected: provenance.attestation.timestamp verification failed (build-host: 2026-03-20T23:02:10Z, signing-service: 2026-03-21T02:00:05Z). See logs: https://ci.redwood.example/ab12
Jordan: Wait — how did timestamp drift that much? NTP issue on the builder?
Maya: Looks like the ephemeral builder VM lost sync during the build window. cosign treats attestation timestamps strictly so deploybot rejects on skew > allowed TTL.
Tiff: Can we bypass deploybot TTL check and re-approve manually for this publish?
Maya: Not recommended for prod. Bypassing weakens provenance guarantees. Safer: pin to previous digest and republish a re-signed image after correcting clock.
Alex: Proposed plan: 1) Pin release/1.24.2 in the rollout manifest to the last-good digest (sha256:af3b2c9d...) so we don't accidentally route traffic to the unsigned one. 2) Hold canary and any automated promotes. 3) Rebuild/sign on a host with verified NTP, then republish and push signed attestations. 4) Update release notes & notify support.
Jordan: How long for re-sign + republish?
Alex: Re-sign job should be quick once we have the proper digest on hand. ETA ~ 30–60m including verification and canary smoke. I'll schedule a 2h change window starting now to be safe.
Tiff: I'll open a hotfix PR to pin the manifest and add a comment in the release notes that we temporarily pinned to a digest while we re-sign.
Maya: Command I'm going to run on the infra-host (example):
```bash
# re-sign the image and upload attestation
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/infra/keys/cosign-prod docker.io/redwood/app:1.24.2@sha256:af3b2c9d...
# verify locally
cosign verify --key ksm://projects/infra/keys/cosign-prod docker.io/redwood/app:1.24.2@sha256:af3b2c9d...
```
Sara: Support note: I'll draft a short blurb for customers in the canary cohort explaining a brief hold while we ensure signed provenance.
deploy-bot: Canary for release/1.24.2 paused by engineers — will resume after new attestation verified.
Jordan: Also filing a follow-up ticket to check builder pool NTP configs so this doesn't recur.
Alex: Good. After republish I'll run the standard canary smoke (latency, correctness, provenance verification) and then unpin if everything is green. Everyone: react with :thumbsup: when you've updated your side.
Tiff: :thumbsup: updating PR now.
Maya: :hourglass_flowing_sand: re-sign job kicked off on infra-host.
Sara: Posting customer note in #support-updates once PR merges.
Alex: Thanks team — keeping the pinned digest and explicit republish preserves provenance and avoids manual bypasses.
